purpose: verify that people using assistive technology and keyboards can complete the key journeys, against a named standard
entry_criteria: Target standard and level are named (for example WCAG 2.2 AA)
Key journeys and a testable build exist
Access to a screen reader and keyboard-only testing is available
procedure: Run an automated accessibility scan on each key page and record results; treat it as partial coverage only.
Test each key journey with the keyboard alone: focus order, visible focus, no keyboard traps, skip links.
Test with at least one screen reader: names, roles, states, form labels and error messages are announced correctly.
Check contrast, text resizing to 200 percent, reflow at narrow widths, motion and time limits.
Log each defect with the success criterion, steps, assistive technology used and severity.
Retest fixes and publish a conformance statement that lists what was and was not tested.
acceptance_criteria: Each key journey was completed with keyboard only and with a screen reader
No open critical or serious defect on a key journey

validation.command: npx playwright test tests/a11y --reporter=line   # example: axe-based checks in the project's test runner
validation.expect: no serious or critical violations on the key pages

validation.check: complete each key journey with keyboard only and with a screen reader and record the result

failure_modes.response: Mark INCONCLUSIVE; automated tools find a minority of issues

failure_modes.mode: Defect fixed visually but not for assistive technology
failure_modes.detection: Retest with the screen reader still fails
Role or name missing in the accessibility tree
failure_modes.response: Use a native element or add correct roles and states

worked_example: ILLUSTRATIVE: Keyboard testing of a checkout form finds that the date picker traps focus. A screen reader reads the error summary but not the field names. Both are logged against the relevant criteria and fixed, then retested.
